windows_side.verdict_independent_port: NOT achieved. The CH340 moved from hub port 2 (previous instance 6&2A2DF978&1&2, removed 2026-09-07 09:11) to hub port 3 of the same 05e3:0610 hub. It still shares the hub, the hub's upstream link to root port 4 and the PCH xHCI with the FT4232H.

windows_side.independent_path_test: a device is on an independent path only if its LocationPaths has a single #USB(n) after USBROOT(0) (no second #USB()), i.e. it hangs directly off a root port; better still on the other controller (PCI(0D00))
windows_side.hub_port_history_note: hub ports 1, 2 and 3 all carry historical enumeration-failure ghosts (Jul/Aug), and the hub has hosted PL2303, CH340K, CH343, an Atmel HID and a Bluetooth dongle at various times. None of the ghosts falls inside a B1Q session window. This is a history of the hub being a busy, sometimes-failing port, not an attribution.

wsl_side.shared_socket_correction: The 2026-09-07 inventory said both devices share ONE USB/IP socket because both vhci rows show sockfd 000003. That was wrong: sockfd is the file-descriptor NUMBER inside whichever process performed each attach (fd 3 in every fresh attach process), not a socket identity. ss shows two separate established TCP connections to usbipd, one per device. The devices share the USB/IP *mechanism* and the same vhci_hcd, not one socket. The plan's design point (adapter-swap alone does not remove USB/IP) stands; the 'same socket' evidence for it is withdrawn.
wsl_side.enumeration_quirk: on the 2026-09-08 21:36 attach vhci first tried the CH340 as high-speed (device 5, 'vhci_device speed not set'), then re-enumerated it full-speed (device 6). Known vhci_hcd behaviour for full-speed devices; recorded, not attributed.
wsl_side.post_hoc_dmesg_session1: the only vhci message between the ttyUSB4 attach (90120 s) and the session window (90701-90716 s) is 'usb 1-2: seqnum max' at 90576 s, which is vhci_hcd's informational note that the URB sequence counter reached 0xffff (the ch341 interrupt endpoint is polled continuously). Not an error.
